summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, a functioning transplanted pancreas, mechanical mitral valve, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for planned revascularization due to a non-healing left foot ulcer. During admission, she developed healthcare-associated pneumonia with fever, cough, and hypoxia, leading to transfer to the medicine service. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin, levaquin, and flagyl, with improvement in symptoms and radiographic findings. Her INR was subtherapeutic at discharge, requiring continuation of heparin infusion at a rehabilitation facility until therapeutic range was achieved. The revascularization procedure was postponed due to active infection. She completed a 10-day antibiotic course for both pneumonia and foot infection, with stable graft function and wound care arranged for follow-up. She was discharged to extended care with plans for vascular surgery follow-up.
